title: The last value wins
idea: If you set a variable many times, only the final number sticks. Everything before it is overwritten. (Numbers only — text as data comes later.)

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

pick = 1
pick = 2
pick = 3
print(pick)
exercises.explanation: Each line overwrites the last. The final value stored is 3, so that wins.

exercises.prompt: If a variable is set three times, the first value is the one that prints.
exercises.explanation: No — the LAST value wins, not the first. Earlier values are forgotten.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

total = 50
total = 20
total = 80
print(total)
exercises.explanation: No math happens here — each line just replaces the value. The last one, 80, is what's left.

exercises.prompt:
You want the box to end up holding 9. Fill the last line.

medal = 3
medal = 6
medal = ____
print(medal)
exercises.explanation: The last value wins, so setting medal = 9 on the final line makes it print 9.

exercises.prompt:
Which value will print?

choice = 7
choice = 4
choice = 2
choice = 7
print(choice)
exercises.explanation: 7 appears twice, but only the LAST one matters. The final line sets it to 7.

exercises.prompt: Setting a variable to the same number twice in a row changes nothing visible.
exercises.explanation: Right. If it's already that value, setting it again just keeps it the same.

exercises.prompt: Arrange these so the program ends up showing 9.
exercises.explanation: The last value before print is 9, so that wins. The 2 and 6 are overwritten.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: 'The box remembers every number you ever put in it.' Are they right?
options: No — it only holds the newest number, one at a time
Yes, it keeps a list of all of them
Yes, but only the first two
exercises.explanation: A box holds one number at a time. New values replace old ones; nothing is kept in a history.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

floor = 3
floor = 7
floor = 5
floor = 3
print(floor)
exercises.explanation: Lots of changes, but the final line sets it back to 3. The last value always wins.

exercises.prompt: To know what a variable will print, read down to the LAST time it was set before that print.
exercises.explanation: Exactly the trick! Scan down for the final assignment before the print. That's your answer.
